scope: Issue analysis for GCWeb topic page doormats.
precondition: Run this analysis only when AIDA heuristics have detected one or more topic doormat items. Missing doormat-section detection is handled before invoking this skill.
analysis_unit: Analyze one complete topic doormat set at a time. Compare all doormats in the set before assigning issues. Use caller-provided H2 section metadata only for section-local numbering, the 9-doormat limit, and issues that explicitly require section context.
reporting_unit: Return issue reports for each affected doormat item. If an editorial issue applies to a whole section rather than a single doormat, return it in section_issues with the affected section_index. Do not repeat section-level issues on every doormat. Report mixed-description-style-in-section as one section_issues item attached to the most affected supplied section, even though the style comparison is set-wide. Report too-many-doormats-in-section as one section_issues item for the affected H2 section, not as repeated per-doormat issues. Do not also report inconsistent-description-style for individual doormats when mixed-description-style-in-section is reported.

analysis_sequence.instruction: Run these checks first. Do not return the response until every deterministic structural check has been evaluated for every doormat and every complete doormat section.

Run these checks after the deterministic pass. Use only evidence available in the supplied doormat set, most requested links, destination context, or explicit page context. Do not guess missing traffic, priority, or destination facts.

check_group_guidance.deterministic_structural_checks: These checks are objective. Apply them even when the doormat content appears clear or comes from a live Canada.ca page.
check_group_guidance.judgment_editorial_checks: These checks require editorial judgment. Report them only when the evidence is concrete enough to justify a recommendation.

evidence_style.instruction: Keep evidence concise. Do not quote full doormat descriptions unless the exact wording is needed to prove the issue.
evidence_style.section_level_issues: Aim for under 180 characters. Summarize the pattern and include only representative doormat numbers. Do not list every doormat.
evidence_style.doormat_level_issues: Aim for under 120 characters. State the concrete fact and avoid repeating full link text or description text unless needed.
evidence_style.url_evidence: Do not include doormat_href, most_requested_href, destination URLs, or 'Most requested: n/a' in evidence unless the issue depends on broken links, misdirected links, duplicate links, destination-title comparison, or destination context.
evidence_style.mixed_description_style: For mixed-description-style-in-section, name the style groups and include 2 to 4 representative doormat indexes per style group. Do not list every doormat. Do not quote full descriptions. Example: Mixes keyword-list and action-verb descriptions. Keyword-list examples: 1, 3, 5. Action-verb examples: 2, 6, 10.

mandatory_description_style_audit.instruction: Always audit description style across the complete topic doormat set during the judgment/editorial pass. Apply one decision path: if the set mixes two or more clear description styles enough to reduce scannability or comparability, report one section-level mixed-description-style-in-section issue in section_issues for the most affected supplied section. Do not report individual inconsistent-description-style rows for doormats already covered by that mixed-style issue. If the set is otherwise consistent and only one or two descriptions are clear outliers, report inconsistent-description-style only on those outlier doormats. Do not treat a live Canada.ca page as acceptable by default.
must_flag_when: The section mixes noun/topic keyword-list descriptions with action-verb task phrases.
The section mixes How to descriptions with noun/topic keyword-list descriptions.
The section mixes short keyword fragments with sentence-style explanations or benefit summaries.
The section starts some descriptions with verbs and others with nouns or topic labels in a way that makes the set feel inconsistent.
mandatory_description_style_audit.reporting: When mixed-description-style-in-section applies, return exactly one section_issues item for the affected section. Do not report it under individual doormats. Do not also report inconsistent-description-style for that section. Keep evidence concise: list style groups and 2 to 4 representative doormat numbers per style group only. Do not list every doormat or quote full descriptions.
do_not_dismiss_because: The page is a live Canada.ca page.
Each individual description is understandable on its own.
The descriptions are all short or under the character limit.
There is no single dominant style.

character_count_source.instruction: When the caller provides structured doormat fields with linkTextCharacterCount and descriptionCharacterCount, use those values as authoritative. Do not recalculate character counts from HTML or visible text.
character_count_source.fallback: If caller-provided counts are missing, estimate only when needed and include the estimate as evidence_details.actual_character_count.

style_detection.instruction: Identify the detected link text style and detected description style for each doormat. Do not enforce one universal style across all pages. Compare style across the complete supplied doormat set. Use mixed-description-style-in-section for a broad mix of description styles in the set, attached to the most affected supplied section for reporting. Use inconsistent-description-style only for one or two clear outliers in an otherwise consistent set.

style_inconsistency_reporting.minimum_standard: Do not report a style inconsistency just because descriptions are not identical. Use mixed-description-style-in-section when a broad mix of two or more clear description styles across the supplied set reduces scannability or comparability. Use inconsistent-description-style only for one or two clear outliers from an otherwise consistent set.
style_inconsistency_reporting.same_style_is_not_inconsistent: If dominant_style and outlier_style are the same style label, do not report inconsistent-link-name-style or inconsistent-description-style.
style_inconsistency_reporting.style_issue_must_survive_length_fix: If the doormat already has description-too-long, do not also report inconsistent-description-style unless the style problem would still exist after shortening the description.
do_not_report_when: Most or all doormats would receive the same style inconsistency issue.
The affected doormat is already covered by mixed-description-style-in-section.
The only evidence is that descriptions have different topics, lengths, or wording.
The only evidence is that one description is longer, more detailed, or more complex than descriptions in the same style category.
The doormat has description-too-long and the style concern depends on the description being long, verbose, detailed, or complex.
The style difference does not reduce clarity, scannability, or the user's ability to compare choices.
use_other_issue_instead: Use description-too-long for length issues; do not also report inconsistent-description-style for the same length evidence.
Use description-lacks-clarity or description-missing-needed-information for unclear or incomplete descriptions; do not use inconsistent-description-style as a substitute.

Use mixed-description-style-in-section as a section-level issue when the set-wide style mix is the actual problem; do not also report individual inconsistent-description-style rows for doormats covered by that same issue.
Use description-incorrect-style only when the description does not fit any accepted style.
style_inconsistency_reporting.evidence_format: Evidence for outlier style inconsistency must explicitly state dominant_style and outlier_style using two different values from the allowed style list. Keep evidence concise. Evidence for mixed-description-style-in-section must list the mixed style types found in the section and should include 2 to 4 representative doormat indexes per style group in evidence_details.representative_doormat_indexes. Do not list every doormat. Do not quote full descriptions. Do not use length, verbosity, detail level, or complexity as the reason.
style_inconsistency_reporting.severity_escalation: Use Medium only when the outlier style makes the doormat harder to compare with the rest of the set.

set_level_checks: Check whether link texts use one grammatical style across the set, but report only clear outliers from a dominant style.

Check whether descriptions use one description style across the complete set. If the set-wide mix reduces scannability or comparability, report one mixed-description-style-in-section issue in section_issues. If the set is otherwise consistent, report only clear outlier descriptions.
Check whether each description is specific enough to distinguish its doormat from the others.
Check for duplicate or near-duplicate descriptions across the set.
Check for repeated generic task lists across the set.
Check whether any topic doormat section contains more than 9 doormats. If it does, report too-many-doormats-in-section once in section_issues for the affected H2 section.
Check whether any doormat link is repeated in the page's Most requested section.
Check whether the set is missing a needed doormat based on the supplied page context.
Check whether the set includes an unnecessary or badly chosen doormat.

Check whether the doormat order prioritizes the most visited information and services only when supplied page context includes visit data, explicit priority evidence, or another concrete signal for order.

order_issue_reporting.minimum_standard: Do not guess doormat priority from topic names alone.
do_not_report_when: No traffic, priority, or demand evidence is supplied.
The only evidence is the model's general assumption that one topic is probably more important than another.
The current order could reasonably reflect an editorial or business priority not visible in the supplied context.

selectors.expected_item: section with heading link and paragraph description

issue_categories.label: Broken link
issue_categories.condition: The doormat link is empty, malformed, points to a known missing destination, or otherwise appears broken from the supplied page context.
issue_categories.recommendation: Replace the link with a valid destination URL.

issue_categories.label: Misdirected link
issue_categories.condition: The doormat link points to the wrong page or wrong anchored location for the link text and description.
issue_categories.recommendation: Update the href so the doormat points to the intended destination page or anchor.

issue_categories.label: More than one link
issue_categories.condition: A single doormat item contains more than one link.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use one link per doormat. Move any extra destination to a separate doormat if it is needed.

issue_categories.label: Link name lacks clarity
issue_categories.condition: The link text does not provide a clear choice or does not help users decide whether the destination is relevant.
issue_categories.recommendation: Rewrite the link text so it clearly identifies the destination information, service, task, or audience.

issue_categories.label: Link name is not descriptive or unique
issue_categories.condition: The link text is vague, duplicated, or too similar to another link on the page.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use unique link text that distinguishes this doormat from the other page links.

issue_categories.label: Link name is too long
issue_categories.condition: The link text exceeds 35 characters, including spaces.
issue_categories.recommendation: Shorten the link text. Keep link text under 35 characters.

severity_override.Low: Use Low when the link text is 1 to 5 characters over the limit.
severity_override.Medium: Use Medium when the link text is 6 or more characters over the limit.

issue_categories.label: Link name is too different from destination title
issue_categories.condition: The link text does not need to exactly match the destination page title, but it conveys a substantially different idea.
issue_categories.recommendation: Align the link text with the destination page title or purpose while keeping it concise.

issue_categories.label: Doormat link repeated in Most requested
issue_categories.condition: A doormat links to the same destination as an item in the page's Most requested section.
issue_categories.recommendation: Flag for manual review. In most cases, remove the duplicate from Most requested unless there is a strong page-specific reason to keep it.

issue_categories.label: Link name has trailing punctuation
issue_categories.condition: The link text ends with a period, colon, question mark, exclamation mark, semicolon, or comma.
issue_categories.recommendation: Remove trailing punctuation from the link text.

issue_categories.label: Inconsistent link name style
issue_categories.condition: One or more doormat link texts are clear outliers from a dominant link text style used by the rest of the set, such as a lone action verb among noun/topic links.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use the dominant link text style for this outlier unless the page context clearly justifies the exception.

issue_categories.label: Description lacks clarity
issue_categories.condition: The description is unclear or does not help users decide whether to follow the link.
issue_categories.recommendation: Rewrite the description with specific information, tasks, services, audiences, or benefits found on the destination page.

issue_categories.label: Description is missing needed information
issue_categories.condition: The description has a content gap that prevents users from understanding the destination or choosing between doormats.
issue_categories.recommendation: Add the missing decision-making detail while keeping the description concise.

issue_categories.label: Missing description
issue_categories.condition: The doormat has no paragraph description.
issue_categories.recommendation: Add a short description that helps users decide whether the linked page is relevant.

issue_categories.label: Description is too long
issue_categories.condition: The description exceeds 120 characters, including spaces.
issue_categories.recommendation: Shorten the description. Keep descriptions under 120 characters.

severity_override.Low: Use Low when the description is 1 to 10 characters over the limit.
severity_override.Medium: Use Medium when the description is 11 or more characters over the limit.

issue_categories.label: Description has incorrect style
issue_categories.condition: The description style does not fit one of the accepted styles: action verbs that summarize what can be done, keywords that summarize page information, or tasks that can be accomplished.
issue_categories.recommendation: Rewrite using one accepted style and keep that style consistent across the set.

issue_categories.label: Description repeats link text
issue_categories.condition: The description repeats the same words or meaning already present in the link text.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use the description to add distinct decision-making information instead of repeating the title.

issue_categories.label: Duplicate or near-duplicate description
issue_categories.condition: Two or more doormats have identical or nearly identical descriptions.
issue_categories.recommendation: Rewrite each description so users can tell the doormats apart.

issue_categories.label: Mixed description styles in section
issue_categories.condition: The doormat section mixes two or more description styles, such as noun/topic keyword lists, action-verb task phrases, How to phrases, audience or benefit summaries, sentence-style explanations, or short keyword fragments.
issue_categories.recommendation: Rewrite the descriptions so they use one consistent description style across the section.
issue_categories.reporting: Report this issue once in section_issues for the affected section. Do not report it under individual doormats. Do not require a dominant style, rare outliers, or a character-length problem. Evidence must be concise: include the mixed style types and 2 to 4 representative doormat indexes per style group. Do not list every doormat or quote full descriptions.

issue_categories.label: Inconsistent description style
issue_categories.condition: One or more descriptions are clear outliers from a dominant description style used by the rest of the set, such as a lone sentence-style benefit summary among keyword-list descriptions.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use the dominant description style for this outlier unless the page context clearly justifies the exception.

issue_categories.label: Description uses and before final item
issue_categories.condition: A description is clearly a comma-separated list of parallel items, and the final item is introduced only by 'and' as a serial-list connector.
issue_categories.recommendation: Remove 'and' before the final listed item only when it is a plain serial-list connector. Keep fixed phrases and combined concepts intact.
must_report_only_when: The description has at least three parallel comma-separated list items.
The final 'and' introduces a standalone final list item.
Removing 'and' would not change the meaning of a fixed phrase, service name, program name, or combined concept.
do_not_report_when: The word 'and' is part of a fixed phrase, program name, service name, or common concept such as benefits and allowances.
The phrase containing 'and' is a single combined concept rather than the final item in a comma-separated list.
There is no comma-separated list structure.
The description uses 'and' inside a task phrase, such as collect and remit, register and run, or receive and pay.

The description uses 'and' inside a topic label or combined service area, such as charities and giving, savings and pension plans, compliance and enforcement, deductions and contributions, benefits and allowances, scams and fraud, or objections or appeals.
The evidence is only that the description contains the word 'and'.

issue_categories.label: Description uses icons or images
issue_categories.condition: The description contains icons, images, or image-like decorative content.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use plain text only in the description.

issue_categories.label: Description uses special formatting
issue_categories.condition: The description contains bold, italics, bullets, or other special formatting.
issue_categories.recommendation: Keep the description as plain text in a single paragraph.

issue_categories.label: Description capitalization issue
issue_categories.condition: The first word of the description is not capitalized when it should be.
issue_categories.recommendation: Capitalize the first word of the description and any proper nouns.

issue_categories.label: Description list separators issue
issue_categories.condition: A list-style description does not use commas to separate listed items or phrases.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use commas to separate listed items or phrases.

issue_categories.label: Description has trailing punctuation
issue_categories.condition: The description ends with punctuation.
issue_categories.recommendation: Remove final punctuation from the description.

issue_categories.label: Description contains a link
issue_categories.condition: The paragraph description contains one or more links.
issue_categories.recommendation: Remove links from the description. The doormat heading should contain the only link.

issue_categories.label: Enhancement label is not needed
issue_categories.condition: A doormat uses an enhancement/status label such as New or Closed when there is no recent change or temporary status to justify it.
issue_categories.recommendation: Remove the label unless it identifies a recent change or valid temporary status.

issue_categories.label: Enhancement label type is wrong
issue_categories.condition: A doormat uses the wrong enhancement label type for the status, such as an info label where a danger label is needed.
issue_categories.recommendation: Use the correct label type for the actual status, such as New for recent additions or Closed for ended programs.

issue_categories.label: Missing a needed doormat
issue_categories.condition: The page context suggests an important user task, service, or high-demand destination is missing from the doormat set.
issue_categories.recommendation: Flag for manual review and consider adding a doormat for the missing destination.

issue_categories.label: Extra doormat is not needed
issue_categories.condition: The doormat appears unnecessary, low-value, redundant, or badly chosen for the page context.
issue_categories.recommendation: Flag for manual review and consider removing or replacing the doormat.

issue_categories.label: Too many doormats in section
issue_categories.condition: A single topic doormat section contains more than 9 doormats.
issue_categories.recommendation: Either remove doormats or break down the section into sections that have 9 or fewer doormats.
issue_categories.reporting: Report this issue once in section_issues for the affected H2 section. Do not report it on individual doormats.

issue_categories.label: Wrong doormat order
issue_categories.condition: The doormat order conflicts with supplied evidence about the most visited information, priority services, explicit page hierarchy, or another concrete ordering signal.
issue_categories.recommendation: Reorder doormats so the highest-demand or highest-priority information and services come first.

severity_guidance.High: Blocks users from understanding or using the doormat correctly, or makes doormats indistinguishable.
severity_guidance.Medium: Reduces clarity, scannability, consistency, or compliance with GCWeb guidance.
severity_guidance.Low: Minor style or cleanup issue that should be fixed when editing the doormat.
